title: The File Class
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of the file class and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—representing file paths—in a small, readable example.
Identify one failure, compatibility, security, or resource-management concern and describe a safe response.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study the file class with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you read and write local data while handling resources, paths, and malformed input safely. In this lesson, focus on representing file paths and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Use Path and Files for modern file operations, choose byte or character APIs based on the data, and close resources reliably. Parse external files defensively because their contents may be incomplete or malformed. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

content_blocks.title: How the pieces fit
content_blocks.text: Connect representing file paths with checking file properties before choosing an implementation. The example is a small, observable case; extend it by changing one input and checking a boundary, invalid value, or compatibility limit where relevant.

items.title: Checking file properties
items.text: Use the standard library type that matches the data: java.time for dates and zones, BigDecimal for exact decimal arithmetic, and locale-aware APIs for user-facing text and numbers.
